subject: Air-gap implications and migration outline
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@arcadiaclinical.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Cory Patel <cory.p@arcadiaclinical.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow up: air-gap considerations from today's call

Thanks for the thorough walkthrough this morning. A few things I want to capture so we have a single record before we loop in procurement: 

- Primary driver: state regulatory guidance requires physical separation for PHI inference workflows for a subset of workloads. We need to understand how Redwood would operationalize an air-gapped inference path and what operational trade-offs (latency, updates, maintenance windows) look like.
- Network constraints: our environment restricts egress to a jump host and requires mutual TLS to any management endpoints.
- Data residency: model artifacts must be stored on-site for the initial 6 months; metadata and logs can be aggregated to our EU telemetry region.

Can you confirm the two options you outlined: a) fully on-prem package that we install behind our firewall, and b) a VPC-anchored private control plane with outbound-only management through a hardened bastion? Also, can you share a short SOW skeleton and a diagram of the network flows we discussed?

Attachment: customer-network-sketch.png (PNG, 1 page)

Best,
Julia Park
Director of IT Operations
Arcadia Clinical
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@arcadiaclinical.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow up: air-gap considerations from today's call

Julia — thanks, this is super helpful and captures the constraints clearly. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Recap of pain/goals:
- Reg-driven requirement to keep inference for identified PHI pipelines physically isolated (air-gap or equivalent certified enclave).
- Minimize developer friction: want near-production dev/workflow parity and a clear upgrade path.
- Tight change-control and limited egress for management/patching.

Two feasible technical pathways (high-level):
1) On-prem bundle (no control-plane egress):
   - Redwood on-prem runtime (containerized) installed in your secured cluster.
   - Model artifacts served from local storage; KV cache and prefix caching local-only.
   - Patching via signed bundle exchange through an internal USB/secure transfer process or an out-of-band Ravello appliance your infra team would vet.
   - Tradeoffs: highest regulatory alignment, longer update cycles, higher ops overhead.

2) VPC-anchored private with constrained outbound management:
   - Private control plane in a dedicated VPC; all inference happens in your VPC/private subnet.
   - Management/telemetry only via mTLS to a single allowed egress IP (jump host) with strict scoping.
   - Supports rolling upgrades and lighter ops model; requires approved egress path and attested bastion.

Immediate asks from Arcadia we can action this week:
- A brief on the allowed outbound pattern for the jump host (IP ranges, TLS client cert expectations).
- A short list of the PHI workflows you want included in the first phase (names + approximate QPS / peak token lengths).

Deliverables I'll send by EOD Tue: 1) short SOW skeleton (sow-draft-v0.2.docx), 2) network flow diagram tailored to the two options (network-drawings.pdf), 3) a one-pager on operational cadence and maintenance windows.

Attachment: sow-draft-v0.2.docx (DOCX, draft)

Thanks — looping Ben on infra specifics and Mina on compliance mapping.

— Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@arcadiaclinical.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow up: air-gap considerations from today's call

Julia — quick note on the infra/ops implications from the VPC-anchored approach: 

- We can support a hardened management channel that only accepts requests from an approved jump host IP and mTLS client cert. That channel will be used for telemetry, canary signals, and signing update bundles.
- For your initial pilot (est. 5 QPS, 4–6k token bursts), we recommend a 2x GPU pool with reserved capacity to keep latency predictable under caching patterns you described.
- Backup/restore of model artifacts needs to be defined: if artifacts must live on-site for 6 months we recommend scheduled periodic encrypted exports to your secure object store; Redwood will not initiate outbound transfers without explicit signed authorization per change window.

I'm available Tue 8–10am PT for a quick call with your infra/security folks if that helps accelerate.

— Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks all — finalizing the deliverables for you now. Next concrete items and owners: 

1) Arcadia: confirm list of PHI pipelines for phase 1 + estimated QPS and max tokens (owner: Julia).
2) Arcadia infra: provide accepted jump-host IPs and TLS client cert fingerprint expectations (owner: Cory).
3) Redwood: deliver SOW skeleton + network flow PDF + short runbook for patching cadence (owner: Chloe, delivery Tue EOD).
4) Redwood infra: prepare a short options doc comparing latency/cost trade-offs for on-prem vs VPC-anchored for your pilot profile (owner: Ben, delivery Wed).

Attachments sent: network-drawings.pdf, sow-draft-v0.2.docx

If you want, we can run a 30-minute technical session Tue 9am PT to walk your infra team through the network diagram and a sample update flow. Confirm and I'll send a calendar invite.
